summary: 100-foot steel fire tower near Eminence on Highway 19, built 1939 by the Missouri Conservation Commission; the only source read ends in 1978 and gives no later fate.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower, with a residence and garage on the towersite

staffing.status: Mrs. Thomas J. Chilton filled in as towerman in 1943 and 1944

events.note: Commission bought steel for a 100-foot tower to be located at Eminence
April 1939 newspaper says the tower was being erected on Highway 19 near Eminence; a 1939 state report lists a 100-foot steel tower erected
640 acres acquired by the Conservation Commission for the fire tower
Franklin County Tribune item (September 1941) says 1,360 people climbed the tower in the previous month
Mrs. Thomas J. Chilton filled in as towerman so her husband, a forest assistant, could fight fires
Chilton completed a second spring fire season as towerman and climbed the 100-foot tower several times daily
Extra bedroom added to the residence (FY1956-57)
Barn and garage reshingled at the towersite (FY1965-66)
Overhead garage doors hung at the towersite garage (FY1968-69)
Residence received new floor covering and its roof was repaired (FY1971-72)
New roof installed on the residence (FY1977-78); last dated entry on the page

evidence.quote: has been pinch-hitting as towerman near Eminence to free her husband for firefighting duties.

1944: second spring fire season; climbed the 100-foot tower several times daily

evidence.supports: New roof on the residence in FY1977-78, last dated entry
evidence.quote: Installation of a new roof on the residence at the Eminence Tower site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1943 newspaper item calls Mrs. Chilton the mother of two children; the 1944 newspaper item says she had three small boys. The story gives both accounts.

notes_for_editor: One compiled source quoting annual reports and newspapers; it has no status entry after the 1977-78 roof work, so current standing and access are unknown. Two web searches found nothing on Eminence's later history; their Coot Mountain results describe a different tower (us-mo-coot-mountain). The 1941 visitor figure is a newspaper's count, quoted on the page; no second source was found for it. Ask MDC for current status.
